subject: Throughput projection & surge containment for on-prem GPU clusters
messages:

Cc: sre-team@zephyrhealth.com

Subject: Capacity planning for Zephyr onboarding

Hi Sean,

We have an intake call next week and need a throughput projection and failure containment plan for the on-prem cluster we'll be running in our VPC. High level items we need from Redwood:

- Expected steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU for the recommended model variant.
- Guidance on concurrency targets (per-node and per-cluster) and p95 latency expectations at those targets.
- Recommended autoscale policy for surge events (max burst, cooldown).
- Network egress limits and connection counts we should be prepared to open on our side.
- Any warmup/cache guidance to avoid cold-start latency spikes during rollouts.

We are aiming for a soft launch on 2026-10-12 and need recommendations by 2026-10-01 to finalize procurement. Also looping in our SRE (cc) — they will be responsible for firewall rules and capacity tests.

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
Senior Platform Engineer
Zephyr Health

On Tue, Sep 28, 2026 at 8:22 AM Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@zephyrhealth.com> wrote:
> We have an intake call next week and need a throughput projection and failure containment plan for the on-prem cluster we'll be running in our VPC.

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I sketched a first-pass projection and attached the workbook (throughput_model_v2.xlsx) plus the current network diagram we reference for VPC deployments. Key assumptions up front:

- Model: redwood-ctl/longform-2.1 (fp16, 8-bit-quant recommended for cost tradeoffs)
- Baseline batch profile: 8 requests/continuous-batch, typical prompt length 120 tokens, gen length 160 tokens
- Target p95 latency: 320ms per-token when below 60% GPU utilization (single-token latency constraints depend on HW)

Quick numbers from the sheet (per A100-80GB equiv):
- Steady-state throughput: ~4200 tokens/sec/GPU (observed under our continuous-batching sim)
- Recommended concurrency (sustained): 6-8 active streams per GPU for interactive workloads; scale to 12 for bursty, queue-based workloads
- Burst window: allow 3x burst (configurable via token-burst-cooldown policy) with an emergency fallback to a cheaper model variant if sustained >90% utilization for >60s

Network notes included in diagram: keep per-node ephemeral ports < 2000 per GPU; expect 20-25 MB/s egress per high-throughput GPU under steady state (higher during KV cache warmup).

Next steps: can Marissa and Laura confirm commercial/contract constraints (burst caps, SLA tolerances)? Hiro/Dev — can you review the autoscale policy draft in autoscale_policy_draft.md and validate the cooldowns and health checks? I'll coordinate a capacity smoke test window with Zephyr's SRE if we agree on the plan.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — nice breakdown. A few commercial constraints to flag from the account side (so the technical plan can be aligned):

- Zephyr requested a hard burst cap tied to billing: they want a protected burst pool that doesn't bill at premium rates beyond 10% of committed capacity. We need to define how burst accounting will be measured (token-second or GPU-minute).
- SLA tolerance: they will accept degraded throughput for up to 5 minutes during failover, but expect no >10% increased median latency during normal autoscaling events.

Operational asks (action items):
1) Define burst accounting metric (Sean/Hiro). Proposal: token-seconds at p50 per-request as chargeable metric for burst overage.
2) Provide a test plan for a 2-hour soak with synthetic traffic hitting 3x baseline for three 5-minute windows (Laura to schedule with Zephyr SRE).
3) Confirm rollback/fallback path: automatic switch to redwood-ctl/shortform-lite when average utilization >92% for 45s.

We should include clear communication points for the Zephyr SRE: how we'll throttle, what logs they should expect (token counters/queue-depth) and a simple kill-switch runbook. Laura — can you own the runbook doc and ops play?

- Marissa

From: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Capacity planning for Zephyr onboarding — technical details and playbook notes

Folks — reviewed the workbook and Marissa's asks. Technical recommendations and clarifications below (TL;DR at end).

- Autoscale policy: implement a 3-stage policy.
  1) Scale-add: add nodes when 5-minute moving average GPU util > 70% and queue-depth > 50 for two consecutive samples. Add one node per policy event, upper-bound steady-state autoscale to +30% of committed pool.
  2) Burst window: allow instantaneous surge up to 3x baseline by enabling local queuing and elastic prewarmed slots. Burst decay: linear cooldown over 120s after surge ends.
  3) Emergency fallback: if sustained >92% utilization for 45s, route new requests to shortform-lite variant and mark nodes for cache-warmup in background.

- Warmup/cache: KV cache warmup is the largest source of transient egress and latency. Plan a scheduled warmup step that replays the top 10% of recent prefixes into the cache when adding nodes (this reduces 99th percentile spikes by ~35% in our sims). See throughput_model_v2.xlsx sheet 'warmup'.

- Networking: recommend the following firewall/NAT rules for Zephyr's VPC:
  - Allow outbound to Redwood control-plane IPs on 443 and 5222 for health and metrics.
  - Reserve ephemeral port range 40000-45000 for worker-to-control-plane connections; keep per-node conntrack < 25k.
  - For throughput tests, expect transient egress of up to 80 MB/s per node during warmup; the steady number Sean quoted (~20-25 MB/s) assumes warmed caches.

- Scaling math (A100-80GB equiv):
  - Single GPU steady qps = tokens/sec / avg_tokens_per_response. Using 4200 tokens/sec and 280 average tokens per request gives ~15 qps per GPU sustained.
  - For the planned initial cluster of 8 GPUs, target safe concurrency of 90 requests (11–12 per-GPU) with a reserve of +2 GPUs to handle cache-warmup and node replacement.

- Failure containment: add a short-circuit in the request router that triggers when queue-depth > 500 for the cluster or average p95 latency > 1.2s: it will begin shedding non-critical requests (batch/long-running) and switch to shortform-lite for new interactive traffic. Log entries will include queue-depth, active-gpus, and avg-util for audit.

Actionables I will own this week:
- Finalize autoscale_policy_draft.md with concrete thresholds and health-check endpoints.
- Add a helm chart snippet for prewarm hooks and a sample Prometheus alert rule (INF-2143).

TL;DR: baseline numbers look reasonable — 8 GPUs supports expected early load with the autoscale/burst policy above. We should run the 2-hr soak with 3x surges to validate warmup and steady egress numbers before 2026-10-12.
